reconciliation.vsOct30Edition: same measures, same definitions (oil only: Crude/Co, CPP, DPP, Chem/Bio; excludes NGLs/LNG; Iranian-origin transits excluded from strait figures only; pre-war baseline = average March 2025 - February 2026). Strait 7-day avg 7,195 (data to Oct 28) -> 5,660 (data to Nov 11); baseline 17,147 -> 17,148 (1 kbd rounding, same window); Total Hormuz Clearance 8,462 -> 8,264 (STS net 1,267 -> 2,604); tanker crossings 11/day -> 11/day (latest day 8 -> 8); Red Sea 7-day avg 3,017 -> 4,436 (58% ABOVE pre-war, was 8% above — the edition attributes the surge to rerouted Saudi exports and record Suez transits of Saudi crude, 930 kbd)
reconciliation.vsNov19BloombergPrint: Bloomberg (Nov 19) read of Kpler data: 7-day MA of Hormuz transits + net Gulf of Oman STS 'eased to about 10M b/d by Nov 10, down from about 13.4M at the start of the month', 'recent data remains provisional'. The primary T-2-confirmed clearance here is 8,264 kbd through Nov 11. Same measure family, different vintage/provisionality: the four preliminary days (1,801-12,827 kbd range) are exactly where the gap sits, and Kpler expects them to settle 1.5-2x higher. The primary edition is the adopted basis; the Bloomberg figure is cited on the site as the provisional read. Do not mix.
